fragment

A numbered fragment has a place of its own in a series. A passage gathered into Nerve takes on new neighbours within the text. A fragment can send us looking for a missing whole, stand on its own or become part of something its first maker could never have anticipated. The Library’s writing on reconstructive memory extends that question from editing a text to putting a past together. Fragment 01 · Reconstruction: A Concept of Memory

Reading note. Jung. The dream study in Psychology and Alchemy brings partial accounts together in chronological order. The fragments in Nerve also take on a sequence. Which features of a single passage become significant because of what now comes before or after it? Psychology and Alchemy, part II, §§44–50
